ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, on the left side there is a common vertical wire, whose lower end is grounded; the upper branch starts from this grounding point and goes rightward in sequence through voltage source E1, current I1 marked with a rightward arrow, resistor R1, and finally reaches open-circuit endpoint A. The lower branch similarly goes through E2, I2, R2 to reach B, but to find the potential at point A, only the upper branch is needed. Reasoning: Take the potential of the left grounding node as 0 V. Along the upper branch in the figure from left to right to A, when passing through E1, the potential rises by E1 = 9 V according to the indicated direction, so the potential at the left end of R1 is 9 V. Current I1 is the same as this direction, and the voltage drop across R1 is I1R1 = 0.2 × 10 = 2 V. Therefore the potential at point A is 9 - 2 = 7 V.
